chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn, from his father, from Uthman ibn Isa, from Mihran ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: 'There is no tyrant except that with him is a believer, by whom Allah defends the believers, and he is the one with the smallest portion in the Hereafter — meaning the believer with the smallest portion due to his companionship with the tyrant.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence for a believer working under a tyrant?
ai.summary: In Shia political theology, this hadith highlights the concept of 'strategic proximity,' where a believer serves in a tyrant's court to mitigate harm for the broader community, a role often exemplified by figures like Salman al-Farsi. However, this service carries a spiritual penalty, as the constant exposure to the tyrant's influence and the distraction from pure worship results in a diminished share of reward in the Hereafter. This underscores the trade-off between active political engagement for communal benefit and the preservation of individual spiritual purity.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Ahmad Bin Al Husayn, from his father, from Usman Bin Isa, from Mihran Bin Muhammad Bin Abu Nasr, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said,

‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘There is no one from a tyrant except with him is a Believer by whom Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Defends the Believers and he would be with the smallest of the portions in the Hereafter – meaning having the lowest of the portions of the Believers due to his association with the tyrant’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ahmad ibn al-Husayn from his father from ‘Uthman ibn ‘Isa from Mehran ibn Muhammad ibn abu Nasr who has said the following:

“I once heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘With every tyrant there is a believing person with whom Allah defends the believing people, and he (such believing person) receives the least of rewards in the next life because of his association with the tyrant.’”
